name: Resident Card for Self-Employed / Business Owners

requirements.blocker_text: Decret 05-322 P-RM, Article 29: a self-employed or business-owning foreigner must provide 'all justifications capable of clarifying the authority in charge of immigration on the means of existence' to obtain a carte de resident -- there is no fixed minimum-capital threshold in this decree, unlike the employed track's employer-sponsored work permit. Standard resident-card conditions also apply: a valid passport, a medical certificate under 2 months old from an approved physician, and a criminal record extract under 3 months old. The card must be obtained within 15 days of entry (Article 31); renewal is possible on payment of the same tax (Article 33). Mali's Investment Promotion Agency (API-Mali) offers general business-facilitation measures -- a single-window company-registration system and 'shortened timelines for permits and business visas' -- but no dedicated investor-visa category or minimum-investment-linked residence status was found.
requirements.fix_path: Register the business and compile documentation of self-sufficient means (business plan, projected revenue, financial statements) to satisfy the immigration authority's discretionary assessment.

evidence_required.document: Medical certificate (under 2 months old, approved physician)
Documentation of business activity and means of existence

outcome.duration_length: resident card, renewable, exact validity period not specified in the decree

sources.title: Decret 05-322 P-RM (hosted via ILO NATLEX) -- resident-card conditions for self-employed/business-owning immigrants, Article 29

API-Mali (Agence pour la Promotion des Investissements au Mali, official government investment-promotion agency) -- confirms no dedicated investor-visa category exists, only general business-facilitation measures

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Mali). STATUS: PUBLISHED -- hard requirement sourced directly to Mali's own official decree, tier 1 (via ILO NATLEX), corroborated by API-Mali's own government site confirming no dedicated investor-residence category exists. GENUINE FINDING: unlike several other countries in this dataset (see ba_investor_residence.json for Bosnia's comparable case), Mali has no distinct 'investor visa' or minimum-capital-linked residence status at all -- business owners and the self-employed simply use the SAME general carte de resident regime as any other immigrant, satisfying a discretionary, undefined 'means of existence' standard rather than a fixed capital threshold. This is a genuinely open-ended requirement -- the decree does not specify what documentation suffices, leaving real discretion with the immigration authority. Shares this country's structural finding (see ml_work_permit.json) that Mali's residence regime has no formal temporary-to-permanent progression -- the carte de resident is the single ongoing status. family_can_work left null: not addressed by either source.
